title: How GraphRAG retrieves connected context
subtitle: Documents become a knowledge graph; questions are answered from vector, keyword and graph search, with sources.
hook: Three or more hops need a graph, and agents' long, exact queries brought BM25 back.

sources.title: RAG Needs a Map: Using GraphRAG to Retrieve Connected Context
sources.speaker: Nyah Macklin

sources.title: The unreasonable effectiveness of BM25 for agentic search
sources.speaker: Jo Kristian Bergum

nodes.label: Chunk and embed
nodes.detail: Splits the source PDFs and CSVs into fixed-size chunks of 500 and turns each chunk into an embedding vector.
nodes.tradeoff: Chunks overlap a little, so a fact cut at a chunk boundary is not lost.

nodes.label: Entity extraction
nodes.detail: An LLM reads each chunk and returns the entities and relationships it finds as JSON, which become graph nodes and edges.
nodes.tradeoff: Giving the LLM a fixed list of node and relationship types stops it from inventing new ones.

nodes.label: Knowledge graph
nodes.detail: Holds the chunks, their embeddings and the extracted entities in one graph, with a vector index on the chunk embeddings.
nodes.tradeoff: Re-running ingestion without deduplication doubled the lessons, so the agent counted 30 instead of 15.

nodes.label: Agent
nodes.detail: Receives the user's question and picks a tool: similarity search over chunks, or turning the question into a Cypher query.
nodes.tradeoff: Graph paths make each answer traceable, which matters in regulated fields like finance, medicine and law.

nodes.label: Vector search
nodes.detail: Embeds the question with the same model used at ingest (OpenAI text-embedding-3-small, 1536 dimensions) and returns the top 5 chunks.
nodes.tradeoff: Enough for search-engine style questions, but falls short when the answer needs several hops.

nodes.label: Keyword search
nodes.detail: BM25 scores each document by how the query's words match its words, so exact names, entities, zip codes and SKUs are found.
nodes.tradeoff: Cheap next to running embedding models, but its two tuning parameters can make it look terrible or strong.

nodes.label: Graph traversal
nodes.detail: A Cypher query hops from the matched chunks along relationships to the connected entities, returning that connected graph data.
nodes.tradeoff: Plain RAG is usually bad at counting across documents; a graph query answers 'how many lessons' directly.

nodes.label: Combine context
nodes.detail: Joins the search hits and their graph neighbours into one context; the retrieval query must return each node with its score.
nodes.tradeoff: The graph adds to the vector layer rather than replacing it, so you get the benefits of both.

nodes.label: Answer with sources
nodes.detail: The LLM answers only from the retrieved graph context and lists the sources the answer came from.
nodes.tradeoff: Because answers come from linked nodes, you can trace and explain how the system reached them.

flow.text: Gets the question: how does temperature affect an LLM?
Embeds the question and fetches the five closest lesson chunks.
Finds chunks that contain the exact word 'temperature'.
Follows relationships from those chunks to connected concepts and lessons.
Merges the hits and their neighbours into one scored context.
Answers from that context only and names the lessons it used.

takeaways.text: Vector RAG suits search-style questions; questions needing three or more hops, or aggregation, need a graph.
Use graph and vector together: the knowledge graph adds to your vector layer instead of replacing it.
BM25 is back because LLM agents write long, precise queries, and exact terms like names and SKUs matter.
